content: The supine position refers to a body posture where an individual lies flat on their back with their face directed upwards. This is in contrast to the prone position, where the individual lies face down. In anatomical terms, the posterior side of the body is positioned downward, while the anterior side faces upward. In simpler terms, this means lying on your back and looking up. During a knee examination conducted in the supine position, several specific assessments are performed. These include checking for the presence of any abnormal masses, scars, or lesions. The examiner also looks for signs of trauma or evidence of previous surgical interventions. Swelling, particularly in the medial fossa (the depression located medially to the patella), is evaluated, along with any redness (erythema) in the area. The muscle bulk and symmetry of the quadriceps are assessed, with particular attention to atrophy in the medial portion of the quadriceps muscle, specifically the vastus medialis. Additionally, the examiner evaluates whether there is any displacement of the patella (kneecap). The supine position is also utilized in various other medical examinations. These include internal autopsies, palpation and auscultation of abdominal organs, and assessments of cardiovascular function.
